title: Optimized method for extraction and purification of inorganic phosphate from plant material
author: Rieckmann, Blake, et al.
materials: The amount of phosphate (µmol) in the sample was quantified before proceeding with step II. Quantification was conducted by ion chromatography (Dionex™ ICS-2100, Thermo Scientific, Sunnyvale, USA) using Dionex™ IonPac™ AG11-HC (2 × 250 mm) and AS11-HC (4 × 50 mm) columns heated to 30°C, with calibration carried out using a seven-anion calibration standard (Thermo Scientific) and four samples of pure KH2PO4 dissolved in 0.3 M TCA as a standard with an analytical error of ± 0.2 µmol/L. The limit of detection was determined based on seven injections of the lowest standard and found to be 0.02 µmol/L for phosphate.

To each sample, exercised DAX-8 resin (Superlite™, Sigma-Aaldrich) was added to the sample in a 1:5 ml (resin:sample) ratio and shaken for 3 h on an end-over-end shaker in a cold room at 4°C. Samples were then centrifuged at 10.000 g for two minutes and filtered through 0.7 µm GF/F filters (Whatman International Ltd.) into new centrifuge tubes using a reusable bottle-top filter. The resin was washed several times until the sample volume increased by approximately four times, which was sufficient to collect all phosphate from the resin.

The cation exchange step followed the protocol described by Liang [4] and Blake et al. [1]. From the MAP dissolution step the sample was strongly acidic due to the HNO3, so the pH was adjusted to 5 by 1M NaOH before starting the cation exchange step. Transfer pipettes with a capacity of 15 ml were cut on the top and the tip plugged with quartz wool. Transfer pipettes were filled with 4 ml exercised resin slurry (Bio-Rad, AG50W-X8, 100-200 mesh, H+-form) and placed in a rack (Fig. 6). Following sample elution, the cation resin was rinsed carefully with milli-Q water to collect all dissolved phosphate.Fig. 6Step V of the purification method showing an example of the cation exchange column setup. Transfer pipettes (15 ml) were plugged with a small amount of glass wool and a large hole cut in the top. Rinse water was collected in small beakers, which were replaced with acid washed plastic beakers once the sample had been added to the resin column.Fig 6

steps.title: Extract phosphate from fresh leaves (optional)
steps.instruction: Add fresh barley leaves to a container with 0.3 M trichloroacetic acid (TCA), macerate for 45 seconds, then place the sample on an end‑over‑end shaker at 4 °C for 1 hour.

steps.title: Sample preparation and phosphate extraction
steps.instruction: Weigh dry plant material and add 0.3 M TCA at a 1 g : 20 mL ratio in 50 mL polypropylene centrifuge tubes; shake on an end‑over‑end shaker in a cold room (4 °C) for 1 hour; centrifuge at 10 000 g for 2 minutes; filter the supernatant through a 0.7 µm GF/F filter into a new 50 mL tube; wash the pellet three times with 2–3 mL milli‑Q water (filter the wash and add to the same tube); quantify phosphate in the extract by ion chromatography (Dionex™ ICS‑2100, columns AG11‑HC 2 × 250 mm and AS11‑HC 4 × 50 mm, column temperature 30 °C, calibration with a seven‑anion standard and four KH₂PO₄ standards in 0.3 M TCA, detection limit 0.02 µmol L⁻¹).

steps.title: Remove dissolved organic compounds
steps.instruction: Add exercised DAX‑8 resin (Superlite™, Sigma‑Aldrich) to each extract at a 1 : 5 mL (resin : sample) ratio; shake on an end‑over‑end shaker in a cold room (4 °C) for 3 hours; centrifuge at 10 000 g for 2 minutes; filter through a 0.7 µm GF/F filter into a new tube; wash the resin repeatedly with milli‑Q water until the sample volume has increased to approximately four times the original, ensuring complete phosphate recovery.

steps.title: Ammonium phosphomolybdate (APM) precipitation
steps.instruction: To each resin‑treated extract add ammonium nitrate (NH₄NO₃) at a 120 : 1 weight ratio (NH₄NO₃ : PO₄); swirl until dissolved. Heat the mixture to 48 °C and add ammonium molybdate (AM) reagent while mixing, delivering a total of 7 mL AM reagent; when APM crystals first appear, continue mixing for 10 minutes, then add the remaining AM reagent. Allow the mixture to stand overnight for complete crystal development. Recover APM crystals by vacuum filtration, rinse with 5 % NH₄NO₃ solution, and dissolve the crystals in a minimal volume of ammonium citrate reagent in the same tube. Centrifuge 1–2 minutes to collect the dissolved phosphate for the next step.

steps.title: Magnesium ammonium phosphate (MAP) precipitation
steps.instruction: Adjust the pH of the APM‑dissolved solution to below 7 with nitric acid. Add MAP reagent to obtain a ratio of 0.25 mL MAP reagent per mg PO₄. While gently swirling, add drops of 1 : 1 (v/v) NH₄OH until white MAP crystals begin to form (initially on the tube wall). After 20–30 minutes add an additional 3.5 mL of 1 : 1 NH₄OH to precipitate remaining MAP. Leave the mixture at room temperature overnight. Vacuum‑filter the MAP crystals onto a 0.2 µm nitrate cellulose filter, wash the crystals with a 1 : 20 (v/v) NH₄OH solution, and dissolve them in less than 2 mL of 1 M HNO₃ in the same tube.

steps.title: Cation exchange to remove interfering cations
steps.instruction: Adjust the pH of the MAP‑dissolved solution to 5 using 1 M NaOH. Prepare 15 mL transfer pipettes cut at the top and plugged with quartz wool; fill each with 4 mL exercised AG50W‑X8 (100–200 mesh, H⁺‑form) resin slurry. Load the sample onto the resin column, collect the eluate, and then rinse the resin carefully with milli‑Q water to recover any remaining phosphate.

steps.title: Silver phosphate (Ag₃PO₄) precipitation
steps.instruction: Raise the pH of the cation‑exchange eluate to ~10 by dropwise addition of 1 : 1 (v/v) NH₄OH. Add 0.85 mL silver ammine buffer per 15 µmol phosphate present. Incubate the mixture at 60 °C in the dark until yellow Ag₃PO₄ crystals form. Filter the crystals onto a 0.2 µm polycarbonate filter using a vacuum filtration flask. Rinse the beaker with milli‑Q water; if crystals adhere, add ethanol and sonicate for 1–2 minutes, then transfer the ethanol‑crystal suspension onto the filter and wash the beaker again with milli‑Q water. Rinse the filtration funnel with a transfer pipette, place the filter with crystals into a glass petri dish, and dry at 60 °C overnight (or until completely dry). Homogenize the dry crystals on weighing paper with a pestle.

steps.title: Vacuum roasting to remove co‑precipitates
steps.instruction: Transfer the dried Ag₃PO₄ crystals to HPLC glass‑vial inserts, place the inserts into quartz tubes, and vacuum‑roast at 20 mTorr and 400 °C for 1 hour using a Vacprep (Micromeritics).

steps.title: Oxygen isotope ratio analysis of Ag₃PO₄
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.30–0.32 mg of the roasted Ag₃PO₄ and pack into silver capsules. Load the capsules into a PYRO Cube elemental analyser (Elementar) in pyrolysis mode and transfer the released CO₂ to an Isoprime100 IRMS (Elementar) for δ¹⁸O measurement. Calibrate the instrument using certified Ag₃PO₄ reference material B2207 (δ¹⁸O = 21.7 ‰) and IAEA‑601 (δ¹⁸O = 23.3 ‰); assess drift and linearity with an internal Ag₃PO₄ standard (Tribasic, 98 % Merck).

description: The optimized phosphate purification method for plant material is adapted and modified from [1], [2], [3] and consists of seven steps (Table 1):-I: Inorganic phosphate extraction using 0.3 M trichloroacetic acid (TCA)-II: Resin treatment to remove organic compounds-III: Precipitation of inorganic phosphate as ammonium phosphomolybdate (APM)-IV: Precipitation of inorganic phosphate as magnesium ammonium phosphate (MAP)-V: Cation resin exchange-IV: Precipitation of inorganic phosphate as silver phosphate (Ag3PO4)-VII: Vacuum roasting to remove intracrystalline water and co-precipitated O-bearing compoundsTable 1An overview of the method for extraction and purification of phosphate from barley leaves for oxygen isotope ratio analysis. A short outline of the optimization for each individual step is provided together with the validation method.
